article_title: Assessing treatment fidelity and contamination in a cluster randomised controlled trial of motivational interviewing and cognitive behavioural therapy skills in type 2 diabetes.
citation: Magill Nicholas, Graves Helen, de Zoysa Nicole, Winkley Kirsty, Amiel Stephanie, Shuttlewood Emma, Landau Sabine, Ismail Khalida. (2018). Assessing treatment fidelity and contamination in a cluster randomised controlled trial of motivational interviewing and cognitive behavioural therapy skills in type 2 diabetes. BMC Family Practice, 19, 60. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12875-018-0742-5
title: D6 nurse training programme in six MI/CBT skills with workshops, handbook, and monthly supervision
description: The D6 training programme prepared primary care nurses in the intervention arm to deliver MI and CBT skills within routine diabetes care. It was developed and delivered by an experienced clinical psychologist using didactic and practicum strategies: "Nurses were trained in six MI/CBT skills: active listening, managing resistance, directing change, supporting self-efficacy, addressing health beliefs, and shaping behaviours." Initial interactive workshops ran over 12 3-hourly sessions with a handbook for ongoing reference, and nurses attended monthly supervision with the trial psychologist plus e-mail support for individual cases.
requirements: Nurse attendance at initial interactive workshops over 12 3-hourly sessions with a handbook for ongoing reference
constraints: The article reports nurses did not exceed Beginning-proficiency levels on several MITI domains despite this programme
target_learners: Primary care nurses delivering diabetes care
target_learning_goals: Cognitive behavioural therapy skills for supporting diabetes self-management
examples: Nurses rated as not MI adherent post-training were given extra training and then reassessed, and were deemed MI adherent upon reassessment
